about: The fish of the drowned kingdom after the user's instruction to use every researched fish as inspiration. Each fish descends from one real kind of fish (inspiredBy, a design note only: the game never names the real animal). lengthCm is [typical low, typical high, record] in cm (a legend: [first landing, fully grown, fully grown]). sizeModel is the BALANCE.size model the ladder implies. place is where it bites: open water or one of the four kinds of place; a giant bites only at its placeName. Checked by tools/sim/roster-check.mjs.

waters.name: The Mossmere
waters.echoes: Still northern waters: European rivers and lakes, a reactor cooling pond, a Scottish loch, the lakes of New England and Ontario.
waters.look: As built: the starlit moat. Its new fish are slate, pewter, rust and ivory, with no glow but the eel's and the lamprey's.

waters.name: Sporewood Pools
waters.echoes: Warm still water of south-east Asia and the forest pools of the Amazon: stocked lakes in Thailand, the tidal Mae Klong, Tonle Sap and the Mekong, a drying puddle in Brazil.
waters.look: As built: the ember garden. New fish in plum, amber, rose and cream.

waters.name: Glasswater Vault
waters.echoes: Cold clear rivers and deep cold lakes: the Amur, a Mongolian rapid, Alaskan and Columbian salmon rivers, a Japanese lake, the glacier rivers of New Zealand.
waters.look: As built: sapphire crystal. New fish in indigo, ice and violet; glows are sapphire, never aqua; the one warm colour is the Wolfwake's tail.

waters.name: The Pallid Deep
waters.echoes: The deep sea: the abyss off a mid-ocean island, deep-water traps and trawls of the Pacific, the rough ground of the English Channel.
waters.look: As built: near-black water, bone, ink and gold, a candle requiem. Three built fish gain real ancestors; one common is added.

waters.name: Rushlight Fen
waters.echoes: Reed delta and dam lake: the Okavango, the Zambezi and its gorge, Lake Kariba and the pool below its dam.
waters.look: A fen of tall lavender rushes above the kingdom's great dam, their seed heads glowing amber like rushlights. Pale birds, black still lanes, and beyond them the pale stone dam with one amber lamp and a black pool at its foot.

waters.name: The Thin Water
waters.echoes: Wide sandy rivers with marsh and a dam: the Parana and the Uruguay below a great dam, the Ibera marshes, the beaches of a Bolivian river.
waters.look: Below a broken royal weir the river lies a hand deep over pale sand for miles, the nebula pink on it, reed islands in lavender. At the weir, white water lit amber by one sluice lamp. Rays lie on the sand like the shadows of moons.

waters.name: Lampmoss Slough
waters.echoes: Warm slow rivers of the American south: the Trinity River, the canals at the edge of the Everglades, the Illinois River, the water below a Missouri dam, catfish dens in Oklahoma.
waters.look: A drowned millstream that barely moves, under dead trees hung with stone-white lamp-moss. Violet-dusk water, lavender haze, amber fireflies caught in the moss, nebula-pink lilies; green only as a trace on the pads. A straight stone canal, a broken weir, a drowned lock gate, a log that is not a log.

waters.name: Pyrefall Gorge
waters.echoes: Himalayan snow rivers and their pools: the Kali, the Karnali and the Babai, a foothill reservoir; and a Japanese mountain stream for its one curiosity.
waters.look: A river stepping down a gorge of stone-white rock. On every step a floating pyre gutters candle amber; ash drifts like snow through violet dusk; temple stairs walk down into the water. The head of the river that feeds the Pallid Deep.

waters.name: The Thunder Stair
waters.echoes: Rapids and falls of the great African rivers: the Congo at Brazzaville, Murchison Falls and the White Nile, a Rift Valley lake.
waters.look: The kingdom's stair of locks, broken: a river falls down pale stone steps in a roar. Spray hangs nebula pink; heat lightning in violet cloud, no rain. Amber signal lamps still burn on two lock towers.

waters.name: The Inkwood
waters.echoes: Blackwater flooded forest, forest lakes, oxbows and narrow jungle creeks: the Amazon near Manaus, the hidden ponds of Guyana, the creeks of Suriname, an oxbow in Bolivia.
waters.look: The kingdom's orchard forest, drowned to its crowns. Tea-black mirror water between violet-dusk trunks, curtains of pale roots, nebula-pink blossom on the surface, amber lantern-gourds that still ripen and drop in. Leaves are plum and dusk, never green.

waters.name: The Siltway
waters.echoes: The great brown river and its deep holes: the Amazon main stem at Manaus, Obidos and Leticia, the meeting of two rivers, the Essequibo, a sunken ferry.
waters.look: The kingdom's barge road: a slow wide river the colour of candle tallow under violet dusk. Sunk barges, one ferry with a lamp still lit under water, pale stone mile-posts. Along one line amber water runs beside ink water and does not mix.

waters.name: The Salt Gate
waters.echoes: River mouths where the sea comes in: the Breede, the Fitzroy and King Sound with their huge tides, a Brisbane river, a Fijian mountain river.
waters.look: The kingdom's sea-gate, left open: drowned sluices, a harbour stair going down into violet tide water, pale stone quays, the stump of a harbour light still amber, and inside the gate a drowned shipyard where the ribs of unfinished hulls stand in the water.

waters.name: Lanternroot Lagoon
waters.echoes: Brackish lagoons, mangrove creeks and flats: lagoons on the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua and Florida, the Bahamas flats, a Solomon Islands village lagoon, jungle rivers of New Britain and Malaysia.
waters.look: A drowned orchard standing in brackish water on arched roots. Stilt houses hang paper lanterns low: candle amber on glass-calm dusk water. Pale sand flats, ankle deep, lavender under the stars; blossom drifts nebula pink.

waters.name: The Waxen Reef
waters.echoes: Coral reefs, drop-offs and wrecks: Fiji, the islands off New Britain, Sulawesi, the Florida Keys, the Queensland coast.
waters.look: The roofs and spires of a drowned harbour town, grown over with pale coral like run candle wax. Sea fans in lavender and nebula pink; at night the polyps open as thousands of small amber flames. A wreck lies across the drop-off into violet dark.

waters.name: The Last Light
waters.echoes: The open ocean: blue water off a mid-ocean island, Cape Point, the Sea of Cortez, the Indian Ocean, the Bahamas drop-off.
waters.look: Open sea. One lighthouse on a rock, the last lamp of the kingdom, its amber beam turning over a long violet swell under the whole star field. A drift line of wreckage and pale weed where two currents meet. No shore anywhere.

waters.name: The Rime Sound
waters.echoes: Cold seas, fjords and sea ice: Norwegian fjords, the coast of Iceland, Greenland ice, Alaskan coastal water, the English Channel.
waters.look: A drowned fjord between pale stone cliffs, sea ice across its head with one fishing hole and a lantern beside it: amber on lavender snow. Frozen bell-buoys, a breath of mist, long nebula-pink ribbons in the sky. Black-violet water half a mile deep.

fish.name: The Belled Matriarch
fish.look: Vast flat-headed catfish, tiny eyes, a mouth wide as a door, two whiskers long as bell-ropes, body tapering to an eel tail. Tarnished bronze; a harbour bell sunk in her skull. Eyes glow lavender.
fish.play: Steady. Authored: take, toll, run, toll, circle, last stand, lift. Slow, immovable; never better than a coin flip.
fish.journal: A bell grew into her skull. She has tolled for the drowned ever since.
fish.haunt: Crown: the Bell Pool, the deepest water. Sign: the pool's glimmer; a toll from below before the take.

fish.name: Thousandcast Pike
fish.favours: Predator: Harbour-Bell Spinner. Known to ignore it and take the plainest bait.
fish.look: A pike half again as long and deeper, heavy jaw, pointed tail lobes. Stone-white flanks with dark upright bars, rust fins, an amber rim to the eye. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. Follows and turns away before it ever bites. Slamming take, two leaps with head-shakes, a run under the raft.
fish.journal: Follows the lure to the raft, looks at you, and leaves. Ten thousand times.
fish.haunt: Old water under the Span, beside one drowned rock. Sign: a long shadow that follows the float and turns away.

fish.name: Hullkiss Lamprey
fish.look: Jawless eel longer than the Wick is tall. A round sucker mouth ringed with amber teeth; seven gill holes in a row, lit lavender like windows. Ink back, stone-white belly.
fish.play: Sulker. No runs: it latches and hangs as dead weight through long holds, then lets go all at once. Spat.
fish.journal: It only wants to hold on to something. Anything. You will do.
fish.haunt: Night water at the Buoy Lights, on the lit buoys and under the hull. Sign: seven lavender points in a row.

fish.name: Dusk Minnow
fish.look: Small slim silver fish, forked tail, big eye. Pewter flanks flecked with rust, ivory belly. No glow; the shoal flashes like thrown pennies when it turns.
fish.play: Darter. A two-second flick with no runs. Lost only as a spat hook.
fish.journal: Caught on a scrap of silver paper. It still thinks that was a fair trade.
fish.haunt: Shallow open water, in shoals. Sign: a patch of small rise rings.

fish.name: Mossback Perch
fish.look: Deep striped body, two back fins, the first spiny. Slate with ink bars, rust fins, a pale lichen tuft on the back that grows with size. No glow.
fish.play: Steady. One short run, then it comes. Raises its spines at the reveal.
fish.journal: Wears a small garden on its back and takes the worm anyway.
fish.haunt: Mid to deep water by stones and piers. Sign: slow single rings.

fish.name: Likely Chub
fish.look: Thick-shouldered silver fish, blunt head, big pale lips, large net-edged scales, rounded fins. Pewter back, ivory sides, rust-tinted lower fins. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. One bolt for cover at the take, then steady. Often spat at the raft.
fish.journal: It looks like a chub. Nobody has checked.
fish.haunt: Shallows under overhanging stone and reeds. Sign: a soft kiss on the surface.

fish.name: Overbold Bass
fish.look: Compact bass, big mouth to the eye, spiny then soft back fin. Bronze-slate with faint ink bars, a rust-red eye. No glow.
fish.play: Leaper. Jumps on the first run and shakes its head. Thrown hooks on the leap.
fish.journal: Attacks lures its own size. It has never once won.
fish.haunt: Rocky shallows and drop-offs. Sign: a sharp strike splash.

fish.name: Rustfin Sucker
fish.look: Long round-backed fish with a down-turned sucker mouth and big pewter scales. Tail and fins rust-red. No barbels, no glow.
fish.play: Steady. Heavy and slow, no runs. Slides off at the raft: lost as a spat hook.
fish.journal: Kisses every stone on the bottom, in case one of them is home.
fish.haunt: Stony bottom where water moves under the Span. Sign: a bubble trail.

fish.name: Milkeye Perch
fish.look: Long perch body, two tall back fins, fangs at the jaw tip, large milk-white eyes. Pewter with faint ink bars, ivory belly. The eyes shine pale lavender.
fish.play: Darter. Quick stabbing take, short head-shaking surges. A pack fish: bites come in threes.
fish.journal: Eyes like two spilt saucers of milk. It sees you perfectly well.
fish.haunt: Deep murky water by day, the shallows after dark. Sign: two pale eye-points; nervous water at dusk.

inspiredBy.scientific: Sander lucioperca (Wikipedia lists Volga zander, Sander volgensis)

fish.name: Weeping Carp
fish.favours: Bottom: Mire Worms, Bone Jig, Harbour-Bell Spinner.
fish.look: Deep round-backed carp, long back fin, two short barbels that lengthen into ribbons with age. Pewter and ivory, streaked as if with tears. No glow.
fish.play: Sinker. Bores down and holds; one slow heavy run. Tests the line.
fish.journal: They have never once said they were not mourning.
fish.haunt: Deep, soft bottom. Sign: a trail of bubbles and stirred silt.

fish.name: Kissmark Trout
fish.look: Long deep-water trout, big head, forked tail. Slate back scattered with ivory star-spots, rust-edged fins, and one round pale scar on the flank. No glow.
fish.play: Sinker. Dives straight down and circles deep in steady surges. Can straighten a hook: spat.
fish.journal: Star-spotted, and wearing one round scar where something let go.
fish.haunt: The deepest open water. Sign: none on top; a long slow drag-under.

fish.name: Gloam Eel
fish.favours: Glow: bites on Lumen Moss only.
fish.look: Slim ink eel, small head, one ribbon fin joined round the tail. Moon-violet lights strung along the flank. Glow: lavender.
fish.play: Leaper. Twists, skips and backs away with its whole body. Thrown on the leap.
fish.journal: Crossed an ocean to be here, and will not say what for.
fish.haunt: Deep water at night; thickest at the Buoy Lights. Sign: a violet glow trail.

fish.name: Reedjaw Pike
fish.favours: Predator: Glimmer Spoon, Harbour-Bell Spinner, Cut Strip.
fish.look: Long arrow body, flat duck-bill jaw full of teeth, back fins set by the tail. Slate-blue barred like reeds in ink; pale scars on old ones. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. Lunging take, head-shakes on top, short savage runs. Small ones throw the hook.
fish.journal: Lies in the reeds until it forgets it is not one.
fish.haunt: Reed edges and drowned timber, mid to deep. Sign: nervous water, then a strike splash.

fish.name: The Drifting Grove
fish.look: A round disc nearly as wide as the raft, with a pointed snout tip, small eyes on top, a whip tail with one barbed sting. Plum back with a whole meadow growing on it; cream beneath. The meadow glows amber.
fish.play: Leaper. Authored: take, clamp to the bottom, blooming dive, leap, run, blooming dive, lift. Never better than a coin flip.
fish.journal: A whole meadow rides on her back. It blooms where no one sees.
fish.haunt: Crown: the Mother's Cup, the floor of the Grove Well. Sign: the pool's glimmer; the float stops as if set down.

inspiredBy.scientific: Urogymnus polylepis (syn. Himantura polylepis, H. chaophraya)

fish.name: Harpstring Eel
fish.favours: Glow: Lantern Lure. Also Cut Strip.
fish.look: Thick as a mooring rope, with a flat blunt head, no back fin and one long ribbon fin beneath. Plum-dark with a rose throat, and three lit strings down each flank that brighten when it hums.
fish.play: Sulker. The line hums before the take. Long coiling holds. Every surge is a jolt: the rod trembles, the lantern flickers, the line slackens.
fish.journal: It hums one note along the line. You feel it in your teeth, if you have teeth.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Gill Harp, among the stalks. Mid to deep. Sign: a glow trail at night.

fish.name: Festival Puffer
fish.look: A puffer the size of a festival lantern: round, blunt, a beak of four fused teeth, small fins, short prickles. Plum back, cream belly, an amber-ringed eye-spot on each flank. Puffed, it glows amber like paper.
fish.play: Sulker. Swells and hangs like a bucket of water. Its beak cuts the line: snapped.
fish.journal: Puffed, it is the last paper lantern of a festival nobody finished.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Veilwater's still shallows. Sign: an amber globe glowing just under the surface.

fish.name: Emberbrood Snakehead
fish.favours: Predator: Glimmer Spoon worked on top.
fish.look: Wick-tall muscular tube, flat plated head, wide toothed jaw, long fins above and below, round tail. Ink body with a broken lavender side band. Its fry are a cloud of nebula-pink sparks.
fish.play: Thrasher. Explodes on a surface lure, then bores for the stalks. Violent head-shakes; fouled or snapped.
fish.journal: Keeps a cloud of pink sparks at the surface and dares you near them.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Puffball Vent (a later sheet), among the stalks near the surface. Sign: a ball of pink sparks with a dark shape under it.

fish.name: Velvet Ray
fish.look: A round plum-velvet disc ringed with pale amber eye-spots, each with a dark centre, and a stout tail with one sting.
fish.play: Runner. A flat slide, then a fast run along the bottom and a flapping skip at the surface.
fish.journal: A dozen eyes on its back and none of them work. It watches you with the other two.
fish.haunt: Mid to deep open water; more at the Mother's Cup and the Gill Harp. Bottom. Sign: a bubble trail.

fish.name: Threadling Eel
fish.look: A finless root-pale eel with stitched amber bands, a blunt head and eyes grown over. Slimy. It breathes air and lies in the mud.
fish.play: Darter. Backs into the mud with the bait and knots itself on the line. Quick, slippery pulls.
fish.journal: Mostly root, a little fish. Often taken for the Harpstring, for one bad second.
fish.haunt: Muddy mid-water of the Pools. Bottom. Sign: a thin bubble trail.

fish.name: Netcloud Fry
fish.look: Thumb-long slip of a fish, big eye, forked tail. Cream with a rose line along the flank. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. No fight to speak of. Up in two seconds.
fish.journal: Caught by the netful. Each one certain it is the exception.
fish.haunt: Surface shallows under the lily caps, in clouds. Sign: a shimmer of tiny rings.

fish.name: Falsesmile Barb
fish.look: Palm-sized round flat silver fish, small soft mouth with no teeth at all. Cream-silver, plum back, amber fins. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. Flat-sided circles, light and quick.
fish.journal: Looks just like a Smilejaw until it smiles.
fish.haunt: Under the caps where things fall in. Sign: a plop and a ring.

inspiredBy.common: Pacu-like fish (labelled 'Pacu' by the official channel)

fish.name: Cindertail Catfish
fish.look: Broad-headed catfish, eight long white whiskers, tall back fin, forked tail. Plum-slate body; the whole tail candle-red. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. Hard take, bullying short runs, head-shakes. Tests the line.
fish.journal: Its tail is the last coal of a fire it does not remember.
fish.haunt: Deep channels and pool floors. Sign: a bubble trail, then nervous water.

fish.name: Lostsea Mackerel
fish.look: Long silver torpedo, pointed jaw of small blades, two back fins and a row of finlets, crescent tail. Silver, lavender back, two rows of ink spots. No glow.
fish.play: Runner. The fastest runs in the Pools, near the top. Tests the reel: spooled.
fish.journal: A sea fish that swam upriver and never found the way back.
fish.haunt: Open mid water, always moving. Sign: a fast straight wake.

fish.name: Downcast Catfish
fish.favours: Bottom: Spore Cake under a float.
fish.look: Huge smooth catfish with no whiskers and no teeth; the eyes sit low, below the mouth line, looking down. Cream-grey, lavender back. No glow.
fish.play: Runner. One enormous steady run the length of the pool. No leaps. Tests the reel.
fish.journal: Its eyes are set low. It has only ever looked where it will sink.
fish.haunt: Deep open pools, mid water. Sign: a slow wide boil.

fish.name: Nightbloom Carp
fish.look: Deep carp with a head a third of its length and large scales. Plum body; at night the scales open like amber spore-lamps. The scales glow amber after dark.
fish.play: Sinker. Bores down on its weight and stays there. Tests the line.
fish.journal: By day it is just a carp, and a little embarrassed about it.
fish.haunt: Deep water at night. Sign: amber points opening below the float.

fish.name: The Glass Sovereign
fish.look: A great predatory sturgeon: blunt snout, wide crescent mouth, shark tail, five rows of scutes. Ink-indigo body; every scute a lit sapphire window. It glows from within.
fish.play: Leaper. Authored: take, leap, shatter-run, leap, hold, leap, lift. Never better than a coin flip.
fish.journal: Each scale is a window with no one behind it.
fish.haunt: Crown: the Fallen Chandelier, the north trench. Sign: a crown of light rising under the float.

fish.name: Prismdrop Sturgeon
fish.look: Long shark-tailed fish, shovel snout, four barbels before a toothless tube mouth, five rows of bony scutes. Stone-white body; scutes like chandelier drops, each catching sapphire light.
fish.play: Runner. Slow take, long heavy runs, then a full breach clear of the water. Slips free at the raft: spat.
fish.journal: Older than the Vault. It leaps to see whether the sky came back.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Well of Ledgers (a later sheet), the deepest channel. Sign: a huge slow bubble trail; a breach far off.

fish.name: Shardspine Eel
fish.look: Thick dark eel, broad head, small eyes, a back fin that starts far forward and runs to the tail. Indigo-black; the fin a crest of sapphire crystal. The crest glows sapphire.
fish.play: Thrasher. Bites, then spins on the line. Backs into cracks and knots: fouled or snapped.
fish.journal: A hundred years old and still angry about one of them.
fish.haunt: Old water after dark: the cracks of the Mirror Nave. Sign: a sapphire glow trail close to the bottom.

fish.name: Wolfwake Trout
fish.favours: Predator: Moth Popper skated on top; Glimmer Spoon.
fish.look: Huge long trout with a flat wolf's head and a wide jaw. Slate-indigo back, ink crescents, ice-white belly; tail and lower fins burn candle-red. The tail alone glows amber.
fish.play: Thrasher. The loudest take in the Vault, on top. Head-shakes, one run for the snag; thrown hooks.
fish.journal: The Vault's one warm colour is its tail, and it is leaving.
fish.haunt: Night water at the Broken Hymnal: the tail of a rapid. Sign: a V-wake on the surface, then a strike splash.

fish.name: Prism Minnow
fish.look: Slim silver minnow, forked tail. Ice-blue flanks, sapphire fin edges. The shoal flashes sapphire when it turns.
fish.play: Darter. A quick flick and it is in. Spat hooks only.
fish.journal: The first fish of a far river. It is used to being a beginning.
fish.haunt: Shallow clear water, in shoals. Sign: a scatter of small rings.

fish.name: Rosefleck Trout
fish.favours: Insect: Feather Fly. Takes the Glimmer Spoon too.
fish.look: Stout trout with a blunt rounded snout and a small underslung mouth. Indigo back, ink spots, a row of nebula-pink blotches along each flank. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. Uses the fast water: short downstream bursts, then steady.
fish.journal: Blunt-nosed and rose-flecked, like something pressed in a book.
fish.haunt: Fast clear water at the foot of the Stilled Cascade. Sign: a rise ring in the current.

fish.name: Duskbar Salmon
fish.look: Deep salmon with a hooked jaw and dog teeth. Stone-white silver crossed by ragged violet-dusk bars, an ink edge to the tail. No glow.
fish.play: Runner. One strong run upstream, then dogged circles. Tests the reel.
fish.journal: Wears the dusk in bars down its side, and is going home in it.
fish.haunt: Mid water in the main channel. Sign: a bulge moving upstream.

fish.name: Redhome Salmon
fish.favours: Ember Roe. Rarely takes a lure.
fish.look: Humped salmon with a hooked snout. Body nebula-pink deepening to candle-red; the head alone carries a trace of faded green. No glow.
fish.play: Runner. Fast, shallow, erratic. Its own got-away note: something bigger took it off the hook.
fish.journal: Turns red to go home. Something is usually waiting on the way.
fish.haunt: Shallow runs near the surface. Sign: a red back breaking the water.

fish.name: Tremor Catfish
fish.look: Soft tadpole-shaped catfish: broad head, two long whiskers, a tiny back fin, a long fin under the body joined to a small round tail. Indigo, ice-white belly. No glow.
fish.play: Sinker. Burrows for the bottom and writhes. Short, heavy for its size.
fish.journal: The water shivers a moment before it bites. It is sorry about that.
fish.haunt: Still deep bottom. Sign: every ring on the water trembles once before the bite.

fish.name: Rainglass Darter
fish.look: Slender fish with a tall sail of a back fin, spotted like rain on glass. Ice-silver body, violet sail with sapphire spots. The sail glows sapphire.
fish.play: Darter. Raises the sail across the current and kites. Light, quick, often thrown.
fish.journal: Carries the last rain on its sail and will not let it dry.
fish.haunt: The Stilled Cascade: fast shallow water. Sign: a sail tip cutting the surface.

fish.name: Pilgrim Salmon
fish.look: Big deep salmon, hooked rust jaw, frayed fins, ink-spotted back and tail. Silver going bronze. No glow.
fish.play: Runner. Long powerful runs upstream and a heavy roll on top. Tests the reel: spooled.
fish.journal: Always going up the river. Never once coming back.
fish.haunt: Fast deep runs, far from the mouth. Sign: a heavy roll on the surface.

fish.name: Vesper Gar
fish.look: Thin armoured arrow with a needle snout twice the length of its head, fins back by the tail. Indigo mail, violet glass fins. The fins glow violet.
fish.play: Darter. Slashes sideways at the bait; the needle jaw rarely holds. Leaps often: thrown.
fish.journal: It sang vespers. It only ever sang the one note.
fish.haunt: Surface of deep water; thickest at the Broken Hymnal. Sign: a needle wake.

fish.name: The Lantern-Swallower
fish.favours: Its own bait only: the Last Candle (built).
fish.look: A deep-water shark older than sharks: broad blunt head, one dorsal set far back, a long tail, six gill slits each side. The swallowed lantern's ember glows through the six slits. Bone and ink.
fish.play: Legend, a sinker (the built set piece): ember surges, the grasping dark, one long run, a still, a last stand.
fish.journal: It swallowed the great lantern. The ember still shows through its six gills.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Bottomless (as built). Six lines of ember-light rising under the raft.

fish.name: Slipknot Eel
fish.look: Blind, jawless, finger-thick eel with a ring of short whiskers round the mouth and a paddle tail; bone-pale with an ink back; a row of small pale pores down each side.
fish.play: Sulker. Ties itself in a knot and slides the knot along its body; a slow, slippery, twisting weight.
fish.journal: It ties itself in a knot to remember something, and has forgotten what.
fish.haunt: The bottom of the Deep, open water, on anything that has sunk. Bubble trail.

fish.name: Pallid Wraithfin
fish.favours: Predator, as built; Lumen Moss draws it, as built.
fish.look: Large head with great moon eyes and a rabbit mouth, wing-like fins it flies on, one tall spine before the dorsal, a body tapering to a ribbon tail. Bone-pale, pearl-spotted, half see-through.
fish.play: Steady. Flaps up slowly on its wing fins like a moth; light, fluttering, strange.
fish.journal: It flies through the dark on two pale wings, looking for a window.
fish.haunt: Mid to deep over soft bottom, open water (as built). Glow trail at night.

fish.name: Gilt-Eyed Eel
fish.favours: Predator, as built: Ember Roe, Cut Strip, the Ferryman's Coin.
fish.look: Thick, scaleless sea eel, ink above and bone-pale below, one long fin edged black from shoulder round the tail; a heavy jaw and two large eyes like gold coins.
fish.play: Thrasher. Anchors its tail in its hole, then spins and writhes all the way up; twists hard at the scoop.
fish.journal: Two gold coins for eyes, saved for a crossing it keeps putting off.
fish.haunt: Deep rough ground and wrecks, open water; the Chain Garden for the old ones (as built). Bubble trail.

fish.name: The Banked Fire
fish.favours: Its own bait: the Blossom Fly, fished on the surface.
fish.look: Three metres of armour. A flat bone-plated head, an upturned mouth, back fins bunched into a paddle at the tail. Dusk-pewter scales rimmed in ember, brighter toward the tail. Amber glow under the gill plates.
fish.play: Leaper. Gulps the bait off the surface. Long runs across the mere, heavy breaches, head-shakes at the raft. Comes up to breathe mid-play. Throws hooks.
fish.journal: It must come up for air, like any fire. It burns low and waits for morning.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Breathing Mere, a hidden pond behind the root curtains. Surface. Sign: a slow boil and a loud sigh every few minutes, where it comes up for air.

fish.name: Emberbelly
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip above all; Glimmer Spoon.
fish.look: A deep disc as long as the Wick is tall. A blunt bulldog face and an underslung jaw with one row of triangle teeth. Pewter flanks flecked like starlight. A belly the red of a live coal.
fish.play: Thrasher. The float chatters, then goes. Tight circles and sawing head-shakes while the pack boils round it. Losses are bitten-through lines: snapped.
fish.journal: It still waits under the kitchen steps for scraps. It is owed a hundred years of seconds.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Kitchen Stair, the scullery steps of a drowned stilt village. Mid-water. Sign: nervous water that seems to boil.

fish.name: Nightcreek Hound
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip; a Moth Popper worked along the bank.
fish.look: A log with a face. A round ink-violet body, a blunt bulldog head, dog teeth that never quite close, a round paddle tail. Pale amber eyes that hold the lantern.
fish.play: Thrasher. Slams the bait under the bank. Short brutal surges, head-shakes, dives for the roots and wraps. Losses are snapped or fouled lines.
fish.journal: It bites the bait, the line, the raft and the dark. It is not angry. It is thorough.
fish.haunt: Night water: Rootgate Creek, the narrow run under the little fall. Shallow, tight to the bank. Sign: one heavy strike splash by the roots.

fish.name: Smilejaw Bream
fish.favours: A fruit bait: the Windfall Plum, dropped where the gourds fall. Ignores lures.
fish.look: Deep round flat-sided fish, small head, and a full set of square, human-looking teeth. Plum-slate back, rose-red belly and breast, ink-edged fins. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. Short crushing surges in tight circles. Bites through line and straightens hooks at the lift: snapped or spat.
fish.journal: Smiles with a full set of teeth. Nobody has ever smiled back.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Overhang (a later sheet), deep water under the fruiting boughs, where things fall in. Mid-water. Sign: a loud plop, then a crunch.

fish.name: Inkside Nipper
fish.look: A hand-deep ink-violet disc with a jutting toothed jaw and one ember-red eye on each side. Fins edged black. Old ones go almost wholly dark.
fish.play: Darter. Hits a lure as long as itself. Quick deep circles and a head-shake at the lift. Always alone.
fish.journal: One red eye each side, like a raft's lamps from below. It knows a lot of rafts.
fish.haunt: Open water and the deep side of the Kitchen Stair. Mid to deep. Sign: none. Baits come back with a coin-shaped piece gone.

fish.name: Windowtail Perch
fish.favours: Predator at the surface: Feather Fly, Glimmer Spoon.
fish.look: A long-jawed perch in dusk-violet with three ink bars and a blossom-pink throat. On the root of the tail, one gold-ringed spot like a lit window.
fish.play: Leaper. Smashes a surface lure beside a drowned trunk. One jump, hard head-shakes, a dash back to the wood.
fish.journal: It wears a lit window on its tail, so that whatever follows it bites the wrong end.
fish.haunt: Open water and the Windfall, tight against drowned trunks. Shallow. Sign: a strike splash at the trunks.

fish.name: Ditch Hound
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip. Cut it and it is good bait itself.
fish.look: The Hound's small cousin. A mottled dusk-brown log a forearm long, with a blunt head, needle teeth and a round tail. A pale stripe behind the eye.
fish.play: Steady. Lunges from the weed edge and hangs on. A short tug-of-war and one head-shake.
fish.journal: Lives in a ditch. Dreams of a creek. Bites like both.
fish.haunt: Shallow edges and puddles all over the Inkwood. Sign: a swirl against the bank.

fish.name: Gourdcracker
fish.favours: A fruit bait (new: Windfall Plum). Spore Cake does in its place.
fish.look: A deep plum-black disc with a pale belly and a small mouth of blunt square teeth, like a person's. It hangs nose-up under the lantern-gourd boughs.
fish.play: Sinker. Sips the bait, then one long dive and dogged circling deep under the boughs. It rarely shows itself.
fish.journal: Teeth like a person and the patience of a tree. It waits for the fruit to fall.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Windfall, under the fruiting boughs. Mid-water. Sign: a rise ring just after a gourd drops.

fish.name: Petal Bream
fish.favours: Insect and fruit: Feather Fly, Windfall Plum.
fish.look: A palm-sized round bream, pale stone silver, washed blossom-pink along the belly and fins as if it had been lying in fallen petals.
fish.play: Darter. A quick take and a fluttering sideways pull in the current. Soon over.
fish.journal: It eats the blossom that falls on the water. Somebody has to tidy up.
fish.haunt: Open water where the current runs between trunks. Shallow to mid. Sign: small rise rings under falling blossom.

fish.name: Gourdseed Minnow
fish.favours: Insect: Mire Worms, Feather Fly. It cuts into good strips.
fish.look: Finger-long and seed-shaped, pale as a pip, with one blossom-pink thread down each side. The school turns all at once.
fish.play: Darter. A double pop and it is in your hand. It skitters.
fish.journal: The bottom of every food chain in the Inkwood. It bears this well.
fish.haunt: Shallows everywhere, under the roots. Surface. Sign: fry skittering.

fish.name: Starback Ray
fish.look: A round ink-black disc scattered with pale amber spots that run right down the stout tail, like the night sky lying on the bottom.
fish.play: Sulker. Slides off with the bait, then clamps to the bottom like a lid. Long holds, short flat runs.
fish.journal: A piece of the night sky that lies on the bottom and will not get up.
fish.haunt: Sand and leaf-litter bottom in open water. Deep. Sign: a bubble trail creeping along the bottom.

inspiredBy.common: Spotted river stingray (Wikipedia: bigtooth river stingray)

fish.name: The Barge-Shadow
fish.favours: Its own bait: the Bargeman's Supper, a whole salted fish on tarred cord.
fish.look: Three metres of grey, shark-shaped catfish. A wide flat head, whiskers as long as the raft, a deep forked tail whose tips trail into threads. Dusk-slate above, pale stone below, small candle-yellow eyes.
fish.play: Runner. A slow take, then one unstoppable run down the channel that tows the raft. Long holds on the bottom. A head-shake at the lift.
fish.journal: It follows the last barge down the road. The barge sank long ago. It follows anyway.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Long Hole, the deepest cut of the channel. Bottom. Sign: a faint still ring, and a dome when it turns.

fish.name: Sternlamp Catfish
fish.look: A broad flat head a third of its length, long whiskers, a dusk-slate back over a pale stone side band, and a tail lit ember-red like a barge's stern lamp. It grunts when lifted.
fish.play: Sinker. Takes hard and bores straight back into the sunken timber. Heavy bulldog surges; it wraps the line. Half its losses are fouled.
fish.journal: It keeps one red lamp lit at the stern, as barges do. Nobody tells it the barges stopped.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Sunk Ferry and its drift timber. Bottom, in the wood. Sign: a bubble trail by day, a glow trail at night.

fish.name: Dapplewheel Ray
fish.look: An almost perfect round disc wider than the Wick is tall, plum-dark and dappled like a forest floor, with a thread of a tail and two small close-set eyes.
fish.play: Sulker. Takes a bait on the sand after dark and clamps to the bottom. Long holds, one slow run, a heavy lift that bends the rod to the water.
fish.journal: Round as a wheel and dappled like shade. It has never been anywhere it could not roll.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Lamp Bar, on the sand under the leaning lamp. Bottom. Sign: a pale round print and a puff of silt.

inspiredBy.common: Discus ray (giant stingray of the finale)

fish.name: Millstone Catfish
fish.look: Short, stout and enormous in the head: a boulder with whiskers. Mottled dusk-violet and pale stone like a river rock, with tiny eyes and a round tail.
fish.play: Sulker. A soft take, then it goes to ground. Dead-weight holds and two slow surges, like lifting a millstone out of a well.
fish.journal: It does not fight. It declines.
fish.haunt: The deep holes where two currents meet: under the Seam and on the rim of the Long Hole. Bottom. Sign: a slow bubble trail.

fish.name: Tallyside Catfish
fish.look: Long and slim, with a flat shovel bill and stiff forward whiskers. Pale stone flanks struck through with ink bars and loops, like a toll-keeper's tally.
fish.play: Runner. Picks the bait off the bar and bolts flat and fast across the shallows. One head-shake on top.
fish.journal: Each bar on its side is a barge it counts through. It loses count and keeps the bars.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Lamp Bar, on the sand bar's drop-off. Shallow to mid. Sign: nervous water over the bar after dark.

fish.name: Silkwhisker
fish.look: A pewter-silver catfish with whiskers pressed flat like silk ribbons, trailing past its tail, and a long low fatty fin down its back.
fish.play: Darter. A quick rattling take off the sand, then darts and shakes. Lively for its size.
fish.journal: Its whiskers are longer than it is. It trips on them and pretends it did not.
fish.haunt: The Lamp Bar and sandy open water. Bottom. Sign: small bubble trails on the sand at night.

fish.name: Vigil Catfish
fish.look: A small smooth slate catfish freckled with ink, blunt-nosed, with long trailing whiskers and a long fatty fin. It arrives in a crowd.
fish.play: Steady. Pecks, pecks again, then a tugging take. Comes in circling with three friends behind it.
fish.journal: It comes to whatever sinks and stays to the end. Someone should.
fish.haunt: Open water, wherever a bait has been down a while. Deep. Sign: nibbles first, always.

fish.name: Tallow Borer
fish.look: Smooth, scaleless and bullet-headed, pale as a candle stub with a lavender back. Pin eyes, a round sucking mouth, whiskers too small to see.
fish.play: Darter. Spins on the line like a corkscrew all the way in. Never alone.
fish.journal: It turns as it bites, like a key. It opens worse things than your bait.
fish.haunt: Deep open water and under the Sunk Ferry. Bottom. Sign: bait stripped fast, with round holes in it.

fish.name: Gill Lodger
fish.favours: Nothing. Land a big catfish and look.
fish.look: A glass-clear sliver no longer than a finger, with a dark thread of gut inside and two pin eyes. Hard to see against the water.
fish.play: Never hooked. It comes aboard in the gills of a big whiskered fish and is found at the reveal.
fish.journal: It lodges in the gills of bigger fish and pays no rent. Murk says he knows the type.
fish.haunt: Riding in the gills of a Prize or bigger catfish of the Siltway. Sign: none.

fish.name: Boathook Catfish
fish.look: Ink-dark and armoured, with a long drooping snout and, down each flank, a row of hooked bone plates like small boat-hooks. Short whiskers. It creaks.
fish.play: Sinker. A slow grubbing take, then heavy plodding pulls along the bottom. Its hooks catch the line: scares.
fish.journal: It catches more nets than nets catch it.
fish.haunt: Muddy bottom in open water and beside the Sunk Ferry. Bottom. Sign: a wide bubble trail where it grubs.

fish.name: Bareface Catfish
fish.look: A catfish that forgot its whiskers. A flat duck-bill head, a huge mouth and eyes set low on the sides. Lavender-blue back, pale belly, forked tail.
fish.play: Darter. Snatches in mid-water and runs in short straight lines. Comes in with its mouth open.
fish.journal: No whiskers. It gets by on mouth.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Seam, and round docks and wrecks. Mid-water. Sign: nervous water where the two colours meet.

fish.name: Hullknock Perch
fish.look: A long silver perch with a lavender sheen, a sloping forehead, big pale eyes and a pointed tail. It drums: two knocks you feel through the raft.
fish.play: Steady. A firm take on a small live bait. Deep, even pulls and a head-shake near the top.
fish.journal: It knocks twice on the hull at dusk. Nobody is ever in.
fish.haunt: The deep side of the Seam and the open channel. Mid to deep. Sign: none. It knocks at the reveal.

inspiredBy.scientific: Cynoscion acoupa per Wikipedia (the freshwater basha is more usually Plagioscion squamosissimus)

fish.name: Waxcomb Ray
fish.look: A small round disc the colour of old wax, netted all over in dusk-brown like honeycomb. A slim tail with one low sting.
fish.play: Sulker. A flat slide, then it sticks to the silt. Short holds and a flapping run at the lift.
fish.journal: Patterned like honeycomb. Somebody down here still remembers bees.
fish.haunt: Silt flats in open water and the Lamp Bar. Bottom. Sign: a round print in the silt; a bubble trail.

fish.name: Lacework Catfish
fish.look: A hand-long catfish in ivory with fine ink lacework from nose to tail, long thread whiskers and a tall first fin.
fish.play: Darter. A rattle on the line and a few quick dashes. Squeaks at the lift.
fish.journal: Far too pretty for the bottom of a river. It goes back there anyway.
fish.haunt: Open water after dark, near the bottom. Sign: light nibbles.

fish.name: Snufferjaw
fish.look: A steep-headed silver hunter with an upturned jaw and two lower fangs as long as fingers, which sheathe in its own skull. Pewter flanks, a dusk-dark tail.
fish.play: Leaper. Hits in the fastest water and is gone downstream. Two leaps and rattling head-shakes. Losses are thrown hooks.
fish.journal: Two long teeth, shaped for putting out small lights. It looks at the Wick kindly.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Seam's fast edge, where the two currents shear. Mid-water. Sign: a strike splash in the fast lane.

fish.name: The Buried Moon
fish.favours: Her own bait: the Lamp Snail.
fish.look: A round disc wider than the raft and thick as a mattress, with a short stout tail. Pale stone, ringed with dusk like a moon's seas. She glows faintly through the sand she lies under.
fish.play: Sulker. A flat slide, then she seals herself to the bottom. The longest holds in the game, slow heavy runs, the raft towed.
fish.journal: A moon that comes down to see the water and stays for the sand. Nobody can talk her back.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Moonbed, the one deep pan in the shoals. Bottom, under sand. Sign: a pale round glow under the sand, and a dome when she lifts.

fish.name: Weirflame
fish.look: A thick-shouldered hunter with a big blunt head, a tight row of teeth and a black bar through the tail. Every scale is candle-gold: the one warm thing in the white water.
fish.play: Leaper. Hits at full speed in the white water. Leap after leap, then runs for the rocks. Losses: thrown hooks, lines fouled on stone.
fish.journal: It jumps the weir every dusk to see if upstream is still there. It is. It checks again.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Broken Weir, in the fast white water under the sill. Surface to mid. Sign: strike splashes, and small fish spraying out of the foam.

fish.name: Blotback Catfish
fish.look: A long shovel-billed catfish, pale stone all over and spotted with round ink blots, as if a clerk had shaken a pen at it. Stiff whiskers and sharp fin spines.
fish.play: Runner. A thump, then a long flat run over the sand and a second run at the raft.
fish.journal: Blotted like a page someone gave up on. It has a spine for anyone who says so.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Lamp Ford, along the channel edge. Bottom to mid. Sign: nervous water at the ford after dark.

fish.name: Inkthumb
fish.look: A stout torpedo with a small rabbit-toothed mouth, pale stone and lavender, with three ink thumbprints down each side.
fish.play: Steady. Nibbles the bait to nothing, then a stubborn sideways pull. Stronger than it looks.
fish.journal: Three thumbprints on each side. Someone is always trying to hold on to it.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Marsh Lanes, and the open shoals. Mid-water. Sign: nibbles and small rise rings.

fish.name: Frostfleck Nipper
fish.look: A deep pale-stone disc frosted with small silver flecks, with an amber wash on the gill and belly fin, and the family jaw.
fish.play: Darter. Snips the bait, then the hook. Quick tight circles.
fish.journal: It bites in cold water too. It wants that known.
fish.haunt: Open shoals and the Marsh Lanes. Mid-water. Sign: baits trimmed back to the hook.

fish.name: Slipwhisker
fish.look: A slim scaleless catfish, lavender-grey with a few small ink spots, a small head, long fine whiskers and a deep forked tail.
fish.play: Runner. A sliding take and a long smooth run down the channel. Often spat at the lift.
fish.journal: Smooth as a wet step. Most people meet it the same way.
fish.haunt: The deep channel through the shoals, and the Lamp Ford. Deep. Sign: a bubble trail moving with the current.

fish.name: Flatbill Catfish
fish.look: A small catfish with no whiskers to speak of, a flat spoon bill and low-set eyes, marbled dusk and pale like wet sand.
fish.play: Darter. A snatch and a few short dashes. Light in the hand.
fish.journal: A face like a spoon. It knows all the jokes.
fish.haunt: Open shoals near the channel. Mid-water. Sign: small swirls at dusk.

fish.name: Grumbleplate
fish.look: A stout armoured catfish, pale stone and dusk-grey, with a row of small thorn plates down each side and saw-edged fin spines that it locks out.
fish.play: Sulker. Often hooked by the tail. Comes in backwards, heavy and slow, grumbling.
fish.journal: It grumbles when lifted, like Murk before his tea.
fish.haunt: Stony bottom near the Broken Weir and the channel. Bottom. Sign: a bubble trail.

inspiredBy.scientific: probably Pterodoras granulosus (not named on screen)

fish.name: Coinback Ray
fish.look: A round dusk-brown disc set with pale spots the size of coins, with a stout tail and one sting. It lies under a skin of sand.
fish.play: Sulker. A flat slide and a short hold on the sand, then it comes up flapping.
fish.journal: Coins on its back and not one to spend. Murk feels for it.
fish.haunt: Sand shallows everywhere on the Thin Water. Bottom. Sign: a round print in the sand.

inspiredBy.common: Freshwater stingray (largespot river stingray per Wikipedia)

fish.name: Thorntail Ray
fish.look: A lavender-grey disc with a fine pale net on it, and a tail set with many small thorns in place of one sting.
fish.play: Sulker. A slide, a hold, then a thrashing tail at the lift: a scare every time.
fish.journal: No sting, only thorns. It is not sure this is an improvement.
fish.haunt: The Marsh Lanes' muddy edges, and the Lamp Ford. Bottom. Sign: a bubble trail in the mud.

inspiredBy.common: Freshwater stingray, a kind new to him
inspiredBy.scientific: Potamotrygon sp. (Wikipedia lists P. magdalenae and short-tailed river stingray)

inspiredBy.common: River stingrays on a multi-hook line

fish.name: The Last Lock
fish.favours: Its own bait: the Wired Bream, a whole bait fish on wire.
fish.look: A huge pewter-silver hunter, salmon-shaped, with thirty-two dagger teeth that mesh outside its shut jaws. Scales like shields, fins flushed ember, a deep forked tail. An amber glint behind every tooth.
fish.play: Leaper. Hits in the heaviest water, hard enough to cut a bait in half. Blistering runs down the chute, leaps, head-shakes. Throws hooks, snaps lines.
fish.journal: Thirty-two teeth and none of them hidden. Nothing passes the lock.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Throat, the main chute of the rapids. Mid-water, in the fastest current. Sign: one great strike splash; a bait that comes back as half a fish.

fish.name: Lampeye Perch
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip, fished as a live bait; Glimmer Spoon worked deep.
fish.look: A humped silver-violet perch with a dished forehead, a mouth like a bucket and a round tail. Its eyes take in lantern light and give it back amber, long after.
fish.play: Thrasher. A thump under the falls and a deep heavy run. Then up to the top, gills flared, shaking its whole head.
fish.journal: Its eyes keep the light after the lamp has gone. It is not giving it back.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Cauldron, the deep pool under the falls. Deep. Sign: a boil.

fish.name: Soapthief
fish.favours: Bottom: Tallow Soap (a new bait). It was caught on soap.
fish.look: A big-headed, wide-mouthed catfish the yellow of old tallow, dusk on the back, with short thick whiskers and a tall first fin.
fish.play: Sinker. Mouths the bait a long while, then a deep rolling pull and stubborn holds. Heavy for its length.
fish.journal: It eats soap and candle ends. The Wick keeps its feet out of the water here.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Soap Landing, the washing steps below the stair. Bottom. Sign: slow nibbles and a bubble trail.

fish.name: Swallowtail Catfish
fish.look: A sleek slate catfish with a flat head, very long top whiskers and a deeply forked tail whose upper tip trails a thread.
fish.play: Runner. Takes on the drop and runs wide. Quick and clean, with no tricks.
fish.journal: It bites best in thunder. Nobody else wants to be out.
fish.haunt: Open water below the stair. Mid to deep. Sign: nervous water when the lightning shows.

fish.name: Cocoon Sleeper
fish.favours: Bottom: Mire Worms, Cut Strip. Villagers took it on a palm nut.
fish.look: A thick marbled eel-shape in dusk and pale stone, with four fins like bits of string and a small blunt face. It breathes air.
fish.play: Sulker. A slow chewing take, then it rolls and lies heavy. Bites the line more than it pulls.
fish.journal: It sleeps through the dry years in a jacket of mud. It always asks what year it is.
fish.haunt: The muddy Step Pools at the side of the stair. Bottom, shallow. Sign: a bubble trail; a gulp at the surface.

fish.name: Cradlemouth Bream
fish.look: A plain deep-sided bream, pewter with dusk bars and a striped tail, and a blossom-pink flush on the throat. Its cheeks are often full.
fish.play: Steady. A polite take and a short honest pull.
fish.journal: It carries its young in its mouth. Never ask it a question in spring.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Step Pools, and quiet open water. Shallow. Sign: small rise rings.

fish.name: Stairhopper
fish.look: A finger-long slate fish with a round bump on its forehead and thick lips. It cannot float. It hops from stone to stone along the bottom.
fish.play: Darter. A double pop in the fast water. Often two on at once.
fish.journal: It climbs the stair one hop at a time. The bump is from the last step.
fish.haunt: The stony edges of the rapids, beside the Throat. Bottom, shallow. Sign: none.

fish.name: Sidepool Snakehead
fish.look: A forearm-long slate tube with a flat scaled head and ribbon fins above and below, flecked with pale stone. It hangs under the surface and gulps air.
fish.play: Darter. A grab in the weed and a quick wriggling pull. Still lively on the card.
fish.journal: The river forgets its side pools. The snakehead does not.
fish.haunt: The Step Pools and every still edge of the stair. Shallow. Sign: one small gulp.

fish.name: The Long Thunder
fish.favours: Its own bait: the Storm Candle, a ball of tallow soap round a hook.
fish.look: A long heavy catfish with a flat bony shield of a head, eight pale whiskers forked like lightning, a low fin the length of its back and a second fatty one. Storm-violet above, pale stone below.
fish.play: Runner. A slow take under the wall, then long stubborn runs along the dam, towing the raft. Deep holds. A last stand at the raft.
fish.journal: You feel it before you hear it, and it goes on a long time.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Dam Foot, the black pool under the dam wall. Bottom. Sign: a long bubble trail; a boil against the wall.

fish.name: Packtooth
fish.look: A lean silver hunter as long as the Wick is tall, ruled with ink lines from gill to tail, with meshing dagger teeth and a forked tail lit ember-orange. They run fifty together.
fish.play: Leaper. A slashing take just under the surface. Leaps at once and again, shaking. Most losses are a thrown hook on the first leap.
fish.journal: They hunt as fifty and are caught as one. That is the sad part.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Run, where the reed lanes funnel into one channel. Surface. Sign: nervous water. Over the Run, pale birds wheel above it.

fish.name: Reedwalker Catfish
fish.favours: Bottom and predator: Cut Strip. It took a steak.
fish.look: Long as an eel behind a flat bony head, with eight whiskers and one soft fin from shoulder to tail. Marbled dusk and pale. It breathes air and crosses wet ground.
fish.play: Steady. A gulping take. It rolls and twists on the line with slow strong pulls, and is hard to tire.
fish.journal: On wet nights it walks between pools. It says the exercise does it good.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Night Lanes, where packs herd small fish through the stems. Shallow. Sign: reeds shaking; nervous water.

fish.name: Foamnest Pike
fish.look: A small bronze-dusk pike with a long toothy snout, ink streaks behind the eye and two little skin flaps on the lower jaw.
fish.play: Darter. Follows the lure in and strikes at your feet. One leap and a short dash.
fish.journal: It builds a nest of foam in the reeds and guards it. The foam does not thank it.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Reed Lanes, tight to the stems. Surface. Sign: a strike splash at the stems.

fish.name: Hingecreak
fish.look: A stubby dusk-brown catfish with an armoured head, feathered whiskers and three stout spines that it locks straight out. It creaks when held.
fish.play: Sinker. A fussy take from very deep and a short dive. Then it locks its spines and comes up stiff, creaking.
fish.journal: It creaks like an old sluice hinge. It is the only one on the dam still working.
fish.haunt: The deepest open water, out toward the dam. Bottom. Sign: nibbles from far down.

fish.name: Basket Fry
fish.look: A thumb-long reed fish, pale stone with one lavender line and a clear tail.
fish.play: Darter. A double pop. Comes up two at a time more often than seems fair.
fish.journal: It likes to be caught by the basketful, by people who are laughing. It misses them.
fish.haunt: The Reed Lanes' shallow edges. Surface. Sign: fry skittering.

fish.name: Blushing Bream
fish.look: A round pewter bream with faint dusk bars and a breast flushed blossom-pink, as if it had just been spoken to.
fish.play: Steady. A gentle take and a short circling pull.
fish.journal: It blushes when lifted. Nobody knows what it did.
fish.haunt: The Reed Lanes and weedy open water. Shallow. Sign: small rise rings by the reeds.

fish.name: The Last Sentry
fish.favours: His bait only: a Carp Cutlet (a new legend bait).
fish.look: A raft-long armoured cylinder in diamond mail, a broad alligator snout with two rows of teeth, fins far back by a round tail. Stone-white and slate; each scale edged candle-amber. No glow.
fish.play: Leaper. Authored: slow take, carry, run, tail-walk, gill-rattle, last stand, lift. Bony jaw throws hooks. Never better than a coin flip.
fish.journal: Still at his post in full mail. Nobody told him the kingdom drowned.
fish.haunt: Crown: the Sentry's Reach, the widest bend. Sign: a log that rolls over and gulps air.

fish.name: Weirshadow Catfish
fish.look: Heavy humped catfish, small head, eight whiskers, a deeply forked tail and a long straight-edged fin beneath. Slate-blue fading to ivory, unspotted. No glow.
fish.play: Runner. Takes and goes with the current in one long run, then holds broadside in the flow. Spooled.
fish.journal: Lives in the push of the water, leaning on it like a door.
fish.haunt: Old water under the broken weir, in the hard current. Sign: a boil that does not drift.

fish.name: Old Portcullis
fish.favours: Bottom: Bone Jig, lowered into the den.
fish.look: Wide flattened head with a jutting lower jaw, small eyes, square tail. Mottled rust and ink; whiskers hang like a broken portcullis. No glow.
fish.play: Sulker. Will not leave its den: long still holds among the chains, then one surge. Fouled or snapped.
fish.journal: It has not let anyone through since the Fall.
fish.haunt: Night water: one den in the drowned lock gate. Sign: a slow breath of silt from the door.

fish.name: Scrapwhisker Catfish
fish.look: Small sleek catfish, eight whiskers, deeply forked tail, a spine in each front fin. Slate with ink speckles, ivory belly. No glow.
fish.play: Steady. A tug-tug take, then a short dogged pull. Rarely lost.
fish.journal: Eats anything that falls in. Considers this a philosophy.
fish.haunt: Soft bottom anywhere, deeper by day. Sign: a bubble trail.

fish.name: Hearsay Sunfish
fish.look: Hand-sized round flat fish, tiny mouth, a dark ear-flap on the gill. Lavender-slate with faint bars and a candle-amber breast. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. Circles flat against the pull, quick and light. Spat hooks only.
fish.journal: Named for the sun. It has only heard of it.
fish.haunt: Shallows over pale round nest-beds. Sign: quick small rings.

fish.name: Startle Carp
fish.favours: No bait moves it much. Insect family, weakly: Feather Fly.
fish.look: Deep silver carp with tiny scales, an upturned mouth, and eyes set low, below the mouth line. Stone-white silver, lavender back. No barbels, no glow.
fish.play: Leaper. Leaves the water at any fright: most plays have a leap. Thrown on the leap.
fish.journal: The sound of oars sends the whole shoal into the air.
fish.haunt: Open slow water near the surface, in shoals. Sign: fish leaping as the raft passes.

fish.name: Tailwatch Mudfish
fish.look: Stout long fish, one ribbon fin down the whole back, round tail, bony plated head. Slate mottled with ink; an amber-ringed false eye on the tail. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. Rolls and twists on a short line; comes up to gulp air mid-fight. Tests the line.
fish.journal: Keeps one painted eye on where it has been.
fish.haunt: Weedy shallows and backwaters. Sign: one loud gulp at the surface.

fish.name: Spotmail Gar
fish.look: Arm-long armoured tube, short broad toothy snout, fins set back by a round tail. Stone-white mail with ink spots all over, head included. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. Nips and carries the bait before it turns. Bony mouth: thrown hooks.
fish.journal: A small sentry in spotted mail, guarding a canal nobody wants.
fish.haunt: Surface of still canals, hanging like a stick. Sign: a slow roll and a gulp.

fish.name: The Ashen Guest
fish.favours: Her bait only: a Charred Offering (a new legend bait).
fish.look: A man-long catfish like a river boulder: wide flat head, tiny eyes, a mouth of backward teeth, eight whiskers, fins trailing long threads. Mottled stone-white and ash, flecked ember-amber. No glow.
fish.play: Sinker. Authored: take, still as a rock, a long tow downstream, hold, last stand, lift. Fouls on rock. Never better than a coin flip.
fish.journal: Uninvited to every funeral. Never once absent.
fish.haunt: Crown: the pool below the Last Pyre, in the push of the current. Sign: ash on the water circling the wrong way.

fish.name: Pyregold Carp
fish.favours: Predator: Glimmer Spoon. Small ones rise to the Feather Fly.
fish.look: Long powerful carp, thick fleshy lips, four barbels, huge scales each the size of a coin. Candle-amber gold, ink back, rose-gold fins. The scales catch light; no glow.
fish.play: Runner. The longest first run in the game, straight down the rapid. Tests the reel: spooled.
fish.journal: Every scale is a coin someone left on the water. It kept them all.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Coin Run, the tongue of the rapid. Sign: a gold flash turning in white water.

fish.name: The Unfinished
fish.look: Long silver blade of a catfish: a mouth that opens past the eyes, rows of teeth, two long whiskers, a fin running the whole belly, forked tail. Silver, ink back. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. A slashing take, then it bites through or cuts the line on rock. The hardest play in the gorge: it lands less often than any fish but a legend. Snapped.
fish.journal: Everyone in the gorge has a story about it. None has an ending.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Boulder Garden, slack water behind rocks. Sign: bait fish spraying from the surface.

fish.name: Pipsqueak Catfish
fish.look: Finger-long catfish, eight whiskers longer than its head, forked tail. Stone-white with four ink stripes and a dark shoulder spot. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. A rattle on the line and it is up. It squeaks when held.
fish.journal: Squeaks when lifted, as if someone should be told.
fish.haunt: Shallow margins and the Alms Steps. Sign: tiny rings by the stone.

fish.name: Puddle Snakehead
fish.look: Hand-long tube with a flat scaled head and long fins above and below. Slate with faint chevrons; fins edged candle-amber. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. Grabs and wriggles. Breathes air, so it is still lively on the card.
fish.journal: Can live in a footprint full of rain. Has.
fish.haunt: The thinnest shallows and side pools. Sign: one small gulp.

fish.name: Almsfed Carp
fish.look: Clean torpedo of a carp, small down-turned fringed mouth, large even scales. Stone-white silver; each scale and fin washed rose. No glow.
fish.play: Steady. Strong, plain pull with one honest run. Rarely lost.
fish.journal: Fed at funerals so long it thinks every splash is kindness.
fish.haunt: Day water at the Alms Steps, mid depth. Sign: mouths dimpling the surface by the stairs.

fish.name: Lampspot Snakehead
fish.look: Long muscular tube, flat plated head, long back and belly fins, round tail. Slate with ivory flecks; one amber-ringed ink spot at the tail root, lit like a tiny lamp.
fish.play: Thrasher. Hits on top and bores for cover; heavy head-shakes. Old ones carry bite scars.
fish.journal: Carries one small lamp on its tail, for whoever is following.
fish.haunt: Slack pools beside the current, near the surface. Sign: a gulp, then a strike splash.

inspiredBy.common: Snakehead (great/bullseye snakehead likely; Wikipedia says 'giant snakehead')

fish.name: The Old Shipwright
fish.favours: His bait only: a Tide Mullet (a new legend bait).
fish.look: A shark-tailed ray as long as two rafts, flat head and wings, and a long flat saw with twenty teeth a side. Stone-white and slate; every saw tooth tipped candle-amber. No glow.
fish.play: Thrasher. Authored: tap, weight, saw-slashes side to side, long tow, still on the bottom, last stand, lift alongside. Never better than a coin flip.
fish.journal: Still cutting ribs for a fleet that will never sail.
fish.haunt: Crown: the Slipway, among the ribs of unfinished hulls. Sign: a row of amber points sweeping under the surface.

fish.name: Sweetwater Shark
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip first, then Ember Roe.
fish.look: A thick, blunt-snouted shark with small eyes, a broad back fin and wide pectoral wings. Dusk-violet above, pale stone below, ink fin edges. Broken wire leaders trail from her jaw, their old hooks glinting amber.
fish.play: Runner. A slow take, then she tows the raft upriver against the tide: the longest runs in the water. Head-shakes at the raft. Losses are bitten-through or spooled lines.
fish.journal: A sea thing that learned to love fresh water. It is not loved back.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Sluice Throat, where the tide pushes in past the broken sluices. Mid-water. Sign: a wide slow wake against the tide; the small fish stop rising.

fish.name: Tideghost Shark
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip. Lights and lures do nothing.
fish.look: Stocky shark with a broad blunt snout and eyes no bigger than seeds; the second back fin almost as tall as the first. Lavender-grey above, ivory below. No glow at all.
fish.play: Sinker. Stays deep and never shows: no glimpses before the reveal. Heavy, steady, strange. Tests the line.
fish.journal: Hunts where nothing can be seen, and has never been seen doing it.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Turning Tide (a later sheet), the murkiest reach. Sign: none. The float simply goes.

fish.name: Inkmarble Eel
fish.look: Eel half again as long as the Wick, thick as an arm, broad blunt head. Stone-white skin marbled all over with ink, like a book's endpapers. No glow.
fish.play: Sulker. Backs into its hole and ties itself in knots; long holds, sudden rolls. Fouled.
fish.journal: Marbled like the endpapers of a book nobody opens.
fish.haunt: Night water: the rock holes under the Harbour Stump. Sign: a slow swirl at a hole mouth.

fish.name: Sandblower
fish.look: A long-snouted silver perch, peppered with small dusk spots on the back, with a soft pink lip. It feeds head-down with its tail in the air.
fish.play: Steady. A sharp tug in the shallows and a strong, even run along the bar. Grunts at the lift.
fish.journal: It blows the sand away to find its supper, tail waving at the sky. Dignity can wait.
fish.haunt: Day water: the Bar, on the rising tide. Shallow. Sign: a bubble trail of sand puffs; sometimes a tail in the air.

fish.name: Brinewhisker
fish.look: A small smooth sea catfish, dusk-brown over pale, with six short whiskers and three sharp spines. The fathers carry the eggs in their mouths.
fish.play: Steady. A rattling take and a dull pull. Always first to the bait.
fish.journal: The fathers hold the eggs in their mouths for weeks and eat nothing. Lift one gently.
fish.haunt: The Bar and the harbour wall. Bottom. Sign: nibbles at once.

fish.name: Tidetable Ray
fish.favours: Bottom and glow: Lantern Lure, Mire Worms.
fish.look: A small kite-shaped ray, pale sand above, dotted with sapphire-lavender spots in neat rows that glow faintly at night. A banded tail.
fish.play: Darter. A flat slide and a quick zigzag over the sand. Skips at the lift.
fish.journal: Small blue lights in rows, lit at high water. It still keeps the tide table.
fish.haunt: Sandy shallows of the Bar. Bottom. Sign: a faint glow trail at night.

fish.name: Kitewing Ray
fish.look: A diamond far wider than it is long, with a stub of a tail and no sting; pale stone marbled lavender, shading itself to match the bottom.
fish.play: Runner. Turns its wings to the tide and kites away in one long planing run; heavy tow, no leaps.
fish.journal: Mostly wing. It flies the tide like a kite nobody is holding.
fish.haunt: Day water: sand bars off the Tide Stairs, bottom, on the moving tide. Bubble trail.

fish.name: Dusk Drummer
fish.look: A long heavy silver perch with a bronze-violet back, a row of pale lamp-spots along its side and a round tail. It drums in the dark.
fish.play: Steady. A solid take after dark, long even runs and head-shakes. No leaps.
fish.journal: It drums for the tide every evening. The tide comes. It takes the credit.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Harbour Stump, under the old light. Deep. Sign: a glow trail.

fish.name: Creekling Shark
fish.look: A slim, knee-high shark: long pointed snout, large eyes, slate back with a candle-bronze sheen, pale belly, ink-edged tail.
fish.play: Darter. Quick zigzag runs and a surface thrash with head-shakes; over fast.
fish.journal: Even the scholars could not name it. It answers to nothing, gladly.
fish.haunt: Mid-water in the tidal channel, open water. Nervous water where it herds fry.

inspiredBy.common: Unidentified small shark (milk shark or creek whaler suspected)

fish.name: Embereye Bass
fish.look: Big pewter perch with a scooped forehead, a heavy jaw, plate-sized scales and a rounded tail. Its eyes burn candle-amber in lantern light.
fish.play: Leaper. Gill-rattling leaps with head-shakes, then a bore for the nearest piling to wrap the line.
fish.journal: Its eyes catch your lantern and keep a little of it.
fish.haunt: Eddies behind sluice posts and pilings, mid-depth: open water and the Chain Ferry. Strike splash: a hollow thump as it feeds.

fish.name: Longlash Ray
fish.look: Round sand-coloured disc up to a metre across, small eyes, a thin whip tail three times its body. Stone-white back, ivory beneath, ink tail. No glow.
fish.play: Sulker. Clamps to the mud and will not lift; then one long planing run. Tests the line.
fish.journal: Wears the river bed as a blanket, pulled up to the eyes.
fish.haunt: Flat mud and sand in the deep bends. Sign: two eye bumps in the mud; a puff of silt.

fish.name: Old Breather
fish.look: Heavy long fish with huge overlapping scales, four fleshy paddle fins, a small eye, and one fin wrapped round a pointed tail. Slate with a lavender bloom, ivory belly. No glow.
fish.play: Sulker. Slow and heavy; surfaces mid-fight to breathe with a sigh, then sinks again.
fish.journal: Comes up once an hour, sighs, and goes back to remembering.
fish.haunt: Still deep pools far upriver, on the bottom. Sign: one loud gulp and a ring.

fish.name: Saltroot Bream
fish.look: Hand-sized deep silver fish, steep forehead, spiny back fin. Stone-white silver, lavender back, ink-tipped tail. No glow.
fish.play: Darter. Quick flat circles. Spat hooks only.
fish.journal: Thrown back by better anglers than you. It bears no grudge.
fish.haunt: Shallows along the Mud Bank, in shoals. Sign: flickers of small rings on the making tide.

fish.name: The Silver Regent
fish.favours: Her own bait only (a new legend bait: a Moth-Wing Fly).
fish.look: Deep silver flank of hand-sized scales like hammered lamp reflectors, a huge upturned bucket mouth, one long thread trailing from the dorsal, a deeply forked tail. She throws moonlight back in coins.
fish.play: Legend, a leaper. Rolls and sighs, then breach after breach with rattling head-shakes and long runs; she spins free at the raft.
fish.journal: She rolls at the surface to sip the air, and the whole lagoon hears her sigh.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Sighing Pool. She rolls at the surface: a slow silver back and a sigh.

fish.name: Snagheart Bass
fish.look: Deep, thick-shouldered bass, ink-black with a dusk-violet sheen; a heavy jaw with dog teeth that pit hard lures; broad square tail; old scars. Eyes ember-amber.
fish.play: Thrasher. Hits like a dropped anchor and bolts for the snags to wrap the line; brutal short surges, deep head-shakes.
fish.journal: It breaks lines, lures and hearts, in that order.
fish.haunt: Old water only: the drowned trunks of the Sunken Orchard, mid-depth. Strike splash.

fish.name: Votive Shark
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip first, then Ember Roe or the Glimmer Spoon.
fish.look: Stocky grey shark with a broad round snout; the whole trailing edge of its tail is ink-black, as if dipped. Slate-lavender back, white belly, one pale smear of candle wax on the dorsal.
fish.play: Thrasher. Short violent rushes and tight circles, biting at the line; deep head-shakes and a last stand at the raft.
fish.journal: The stilt village feeds it and asks nothing. It is not sure it likes being loved.
fish.haunt: Night water only: the Stilt Shrine, the channel under the offering posts, mid-depth. Strike splash.

fish.name: Rootjaw Catfish
fish.look: Very long flat-sided catfish, a jaw that opens past the eyes, two long whiskers, a tiny back fin, a fin along the whole belly, forked tail. Plum-silver, cream belly. No glow.
fish.play: Sinker. Seizes and turns for the drowned stalks, wrapping the line round them. Fouled.
fish.journal: Lengthwise it just goes on and on, like a wet season.
fish.haunt: Night water: the Monsoon Cut (a later sheet), among sunken trunks. Sign: a slow swirl beside timber; a mauled bait.

fish.name: Frownlip Mullet
fish.look: Blunt-headed pewter torpedo with a thick, frilled upper lip, two small dorsals and a forked tail; lavender sheen, one ink spot at the fin root.
fish.play: Darter. Skittering dashes and one flat skip across the surface; soft mouth, quick play.
fish.journal: It looks disappointed in you. It looks disappointed in everyone.
fish.haunt: Surface schools over sand among the roots, open water. Nervous water; one fish in the school always jumps.

fish.name: Rootshade Snapper
fish.look: Slate perch with a dusky rose wash, an ink stripe through the eye, two small dog teeth and nebula-pink fin edges.
fish.play: Darter. A sharp dive for the roots at once, then quick rattling tugs.
fish.journal: It lives in the shade of the roots and takes everything personally.
fish.haunt: Under root arches and stilt posts, shallow to mid, open water. Rise ring at dusk.

fish.name: Flicker Trevally
fish.look: A hand-sized silver disc of a fish: steep forehead, sickle fins, forked tail, a row of small plates before the tail. Flashes lavender; amber fin tips.
fish.play: Darter. Turns side-on and pulls in tight, fast circles; the line buzzes.
fish.journal: A school of them turns at once, like one thought changing its mind.
fish.haunt: Mid-water schools in the lagoon's open water. Nervous water.

fish.name: Sandghost
fish.look: Pale stone-silver torpedo that mirrors the sand; cone snout over an underslung mouth, deeply forked tail, faint lavender bars across the back.
fish.play: Runner. One blistering first run far across the flat, then a shorter second; it never leaps.
fish.journal: You see its shadow first. Often that is all you see.
fish.haunt: Day water only: the Bright Flats, ankle-deep. Tails tipping above the surface and puffs of silt (a bubble trail).

fish.name: Wide-Eyed Stray
fish.favours: Predator: Glimmer Spoon, Cut Strip; the Moth Popper at night.
fish.look: A deep silver sea fish with a huge round eye, a blunt forehead, a keel of small plates before the tail and a scythe tail washed amber.
fish.play: Runner. Hits hard and pulls in wide, tireless circles, broadside all the way.
fish.journal: A sea fish ten miles inland, eyes wide, sure the sea is round the next bend.
fish.haunt: Deep channels far up the lagoon, mid-water. Sign: nervous water in the creek mouths.

fish.name: Harbourdrum Grouper
fish.look: A barrel of a fish: wide flat head, tiny eyes, cavernous mouth, every fin rounded; pale stone and amber-brown, freckled with ink spots and faint bars.
fish.play: Sinker. One unstoppable dive for its hollow to wrap the roots, then dead weight; short and very heavy.
fish.journal: It booms like a drum under the roots. Nobody has asked it to stop.
fish.haunt: Old water: the deepest hollow of the Sunken Orchard, bottom. A boil. Its boom carries across the lagoon at night.

fish.name: Stiltshadow Shark
fish.look: The plain, classic shark outline: rounded snout, large eyes, sickle pectorals with dusky tips; dusk-grey above, pale stone below, a faint lavender band on the flank.
fish.play: Runner. Fast surface runs with the fin showing, rolling on the line; the reel runs hot.
fish.journal: It patrols under the stilt houses and knows every floorboard from below.
fish.haunt: Channels between the stilt houses, mid-water: open water at night and the Stilt Shrine. Strike splash; a fin cutting the surface.

fish.name: The Waxen Abbot
fish.favours: Its own bait only (a new legend bait: a Lantern-Fry, one live lit fish).
fish.look: A fish the size of a cellar door: vast mouth, thick lips, tiny eyes, rounded fins; pale stone mottled dusk-violet, fins amber-yellow like old wax. Coral grows on its brow like a mitre.
fish.play: Legend, a sinker. Inhales the bait and bores for the cellar; immense slow surges, wraps on the wreck, long stills, a last stand.
fish.journal: It opens its mouth and the reef leans in. It has swallowed bigger than you.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Abbot's Cellar, the hold of the wreck on the drop-off, bottom. A boil that lifts the whole pool.

fish.name: Anvil Trevally
fish.look: Deep, steel-plated jack with a steep blunt forehead like an anvil, sickle fins and a hard keel of plates before the tail; pewter going to ink with age, lavender flecks.
fish.play: Runner. A surface explosion, a brutal straight run for the reef edge, then heavy side-on circles; a last stand.
fish.journal: It hits the surface like a dropped anvil and expects the sea to apologise.
fish.haunt: Old water only: the drop-off beside the Broken Keel, surface to mid, on the running tide. Strike splash, the loudest on the reef.

fish.name: Spirewatch Pike
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip first, then Ember Roe or the Glimmer Spoon.
fish.look: A long silver lance of a pike: flat-topped head, jutting underjaw full of fangs, scattered ink blots on the lower flank, forked dark tail. A pale glint runs its length.
fish.play: Leaper. One searing run, then long greyhounding leaps with open jaws; slashing head-shakes at the raft.
fish.journal: It hangs beside the drowned spire for hours, perfectly still, judging.
fish.haunt: Old water: the Drowned Spire (a later sheet), hanging beside the spire in mid-water. Sign: a still silver line under the surface, then a strike splash.

fish.name: Mothlance Gar
fish.favours: Predator; the Moth Popper at night; best on a proposed new lure, the Unpicked Rope.
fish.look: Arm-thin body and a long needle beak of fine teeth, fins set far back like arrow flights; silver-lavender with a dusk-violet stripe, the beak tip faintly amber.
fish.play: Leaper. Skips and tail-walks toward any light, then needle-fast runs; its bony beak shrugs off hooks.
fish.journal: It flies at lanterns like a moth, only narrower and much faster.
fish.haunt: Night water only: Lamp Row, at the surface, where the drowned lamps still burn. Rise rings in a line.

fish.name: Waxdrop Damsel
fish.look: Thumb-long oval reef fish, pale stone with one nebula-pink drop on each flank and lavender fin edges; forked tail.
fish.play: Darter. Tiny dashes back toward the coral; a moment's play.
fish.journal: Each keeps one coral chimney and defends it against the entire sea.
fish.haunt: Coral heads in the shallows: open water and the Chimney Gardens. Rise ring.

fish.name: Amberside Snapper
fish.look: Bronze-amber snapper, each scale with a darker spot so the flank reads as fine lines; one ink blotch high on the back; pale stone belly.
fish.play: Steady. Honest head-down pulls and one dive for the coral.
fish.journal: The colour of candlelight on a wall. It does not know it is pretty.
fish.haunt: Reef edges and channels, mid-depth, open water. Strike splash at dusk.

fish.name: Pebble Grouper
fish.look: Squat, big-mouthed little grouper, pale stone freckled all over with rust-amber spots; rounded tail; two ink saddles on the back.
fish.play: Sinker. Grabs and dives into the nearest crack, wedges there, then pops free.
fish.journal: It takes the first cast of every evening. Somebody has to.
fish.haunt: Rock and coral cracks in the shallows, bottom, open water. Bubble trail.

fish.name: Nebula Trout
fish.look: Long-bodied grouper shape with a square tail and a wide mouth; nebula pink, sown all over with small pale-lavender star spots.
fish.play: Darter. A hard first lunge for the ledge, then head-shakes; clean and quick.
fish.journal: Pink as the far nebula, spotted with its stars, and hiding under a ledge.
fish.haunt: Day water: ledges of the Chimney Gardens and the reef edge, mid-depth. Nervous water.

fish.name: Picket Pike
fish.look: Slim silver pike of the reef with a jutting underjaw, fang teeth, dark chevron bars along the back and a forked ink tail.
fish.play: Darter. A fast straight run, one skip at the surface, sharp head-shakes.
fish.journal: They hang in a row along the reef like a fence that bites.
fish.haunt: Schools standing in mid-water along the reef edge, open water. Strike splash.

fish.name: Cabin Grouper
fish.look: Heavy, slab-sided grouper, dusk-violet with paler lavender marbling, thick lips and a rounded tail; fin edges a thin line of amber.
fish.play: Sinker. A slow, heavy dive back into the wreck to wrap the timbers, then dead weight.
fish.journal: It has moved into the captain's cabin and changed nothing.
fish.haunt: Old water: inside the Broken Keel, bottom. Bubble trail; a boil for the big ones.

fish.name: The Jetsam Shark
fish.favours: Its own bait only (a new legend bait: the Lighthouse Ration, a whole salted fish hung from a lamp-chain).
fish.look: Huge shark with a broad square snout, big dark eyes and a long upper tail lobe; slate-violet back crossed by faded ink bars like candle shadows; pale belly.
fish.play: Legend, a runner. Slow, wide, unstoppable circles and a long tow; heavy rolling head-shakes, a pass under the raft, two last stands.
fish.journal: It has swallowed half the kingdom's lost things, and kept them all.
fish.haunt: The crown: the Unlit Mile, beyond the reach of the beam. Surface to mid. Sign: a tall fin crossing the last of the light.

fish.name: Nightsail Lancer
fish.favours: Predator: Cut Strip first, then Ember Roe or the Glimmer Spoon.
